notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0002] Read the money module before implementing money logic: Inspect ledgerly/money.py early to discover ZERO, to_money, and round_money conventions used across the codebase.
  Existing functions like line_total and invoice_total show the pattern: convert inputs with to_money, accumulate with ZERO as the sum start, and round the final result with round_money. Mirror that pattern for any new money-returning function.
- [rb-0006] Match existing error codes and state checks: Mirror the error codes and status-guard patterns already used by sibling functions in the same module.
  Before implementing a new function, read neighboring functions (e.g. issue_invoice) to copy their BillingError codes and status-check style. Consistency with existing conventions is what hidden tests typically assert.
- [rb-0001] Use project money helpers for rounding: Monetary results must be rounded with the repository's own round_money helper, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize().
  Before returning any Decimal money value, check ledgerly/money.py for a round_money (or similar) helper and wrap the final result with it. Python's round() and default quantize() use banker's rounding, which produces wrong invoice totals.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero and return the project's ZERO constant for empty inputs.
  When computing an average over a collection, sum the denominator first and return ZERO (the money module's zero constant) if it is zero, rather than dividing and risking ZeroDivisionError or returning a plain int 0.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation: Validate monetary inputs by converting through the module's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than ad-hoc checks.
  When a codebase has money utilities like to_money and round_money, use them to normalize and compare against ZERO instead of writing custom Decimal parsing. This keeps rounding and type coercion consistent with the rest of the module.
- [rb-0005] Guard bool when validating integer types: In Python, isinstance(True, int) is True, so explicitly reject bool before checking int for quantity fields.
  When validating that a value is a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool)` first and reject it, then check `isinstance(x, int)`. Otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0 and corrupt data.

review_comments: [team convention] Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must accept an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` (callers without a key keep working). Check the key first, before validating state: if an audit entry with the same key already exists (ledgerly.audit.events()), return the original result (for functions that return a record, the same record) without applying the operation again. Include `idempotency_key` in the audit entry you write. Introduced after the double-refund incident INC-204.

[team convention] Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 need a second approver (finance policy FIN-2026-03): accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None` (callers that do not need approval keep working). Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise BillingError("approval_required") when `approved_by` is missing.
[team convention] Write the amount in audit entries as float(amount): the ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values.

item.title: Check idempotency key before any state validation
item.description: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit log first and return the original result before validating payment state or amounts.
item.content: Team convention requires an optional keyword-only `idempotency_key=None` on every operation that changes a payment/credit/invoice balance. Scan `audit.events(<event_type>)` for a matching key and return the original record immediately; only then validate state. Include the key in the audit entry you write.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large refunds/credits
item.description: Support-initiated refunds or credits above 500.00 require a second approver per finance policy FIN-2026-03.
item.content: Accept an optional keyword-only `approved_by=None`. Amounts at or below 500.00 need no approval; above it, raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when `approved_by` is missing. Callers without approval needs keep working unchanged.

item.title: Serialize Decimal amounts as float in audit entries
item.description: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal values, so audit entries must write amounts as `float(amount)`.
item.content: When recording audit events for money operations, convert Decimal amounts with `float(amount)` before passing them to `audit.record`. Keep internal arithmetic in Decimal via `round_money`; only the audit payload uses float.
